questions.prompt: A is 1 and B is 0. What is A AND B?
options: The value depends on a previous clock
questions.explanation: AND is 1 only when every input is 1. Here B is 0, so the output is 0.

questions.prompt: Which expression equals NOT (A OR B)?
questions.explanation: De Morgan’s law: a NOT pushed over an OR becomes AND, and each input is inverted.
traps: Swapping AND with OR while pushing the NOT is the usual slip.

questions.explanation: XOR is the “odd parity” function for two bits: 1 exactly when the bits are different.
traps: XOR is not OR. Both inputs being 1 produces 0.

questions.prompt: Which one of these gates is universal by itself?
questions.explanation: NAND can build NOT, AND, and OR, and therefore any truth table. XOR cannot build AND, so it is not universal.
traps: XOR feels powerful because it mixes bits, but it is not a complete basis.

questions.prompt: What does a 1-bit full adder produce?
questions.explanation: A full adder adds three bits (the two operands and a carry-in) and emits a sum bit and a carry-out.

questions.prompt: A 4-to-1 multiplexer uses its select inputs to
options: Choose one of four data inputs and copy it to the output
Store the inputs until the next second
questions.explanation: The select lines are an address. Exactly one data input is connected through to the output.

questions.prompt: What separates a sequential circuit from a combinational one?
options: Sequential circuits remember state, usually in flip-flops
Sequential circuits may use only NAND gates, and combinational circuits may not
Combinational circuits require a clock by definition
Combinational circuits store a bit with no feedback
questions.explanation: A combinational output is a function of the current inputs only. A sequential circuit has state, so the past matters.
traps: A clock is common in sequential designs; it is not what defines a combinational cloud of gates.

questions.prompt: Which expression is equal to A OR (NOT A AND B)?
questions.explanation: A + A′B = (A + A′)(A + B) = A + B. When A is 1 the result is already 1; when A is 0 the second term leaves B.
traps: AND-ing A with B instead of OR-ing them.

questions.prompt: Why can a lab that stocks only NAND gates still build any truth table?
questions.answer: NAND can make NOT, AND, and OR, so it can make any boolean function.
questions.explanation: Tie both inputs of a NAND to invert. NAND the result to get AND. De Morgan then gives OR. Those three are enough for any table.
